topics.concept: An MCP tool server exposes functions that AI clients can call: each tool declares a name, description, and JSON input schema, and the server validates arguments before executing the handler. Tool discovery happens through a list call, and results return as content blocks. The simulator implements a tool registry with schema validation on seeded tool definitions.
topics.data_idea: Defines seeded tools with JSON schemas and validates argument sets, recording call logs and validation errors per tool.
topics.name: MCP Tool Server
topics.real_world_use: Assistant platforms expose file, search, and database tools to agents through tool servers.

topics.concept: MCP resources expose data sources like files and documents through URIs: clients list available resources, read their contents, and subscribe to change notifications. Templates let servers expose parameterized URIs such as log files by date. The simulator serves seeded in-memory resources with template expansion.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded text resources under template URIs and exercises list, read, and subscribe operations with change events.
topics.name: MCP Resource Server
topics.real_world_use: Coding assistants read project files through resource servers.

topics.concept: MCP prompts are reusable server-side prompt templates: clients list them, fetch one with arguments, and receive a ready-made message sequence. This keeps prompt engineering centralized on the server instead of scattered across clients. The simulator renders seeded templates with argument substitution and validation.
topics.data_idea: Defines seeded prompt templates with required and optional arguments and renders them, tracking missing-argument errors.
topics.name: MCP Prompt Template Server
topics.real_world_use: Teams centralize system prompts as server templates for consistent agent behavior.

topics.concept: MCP clients speak JSON-RPC 2.0: requests carry method names and params with IDs, responses return results or errors, and notifications are one-way. The client simulator builds requests, matches responses by ID, and handles timeouts and error codes. Batching multiple requests in one message cuts round trips.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded JSON-RPC request batches with injected errors and timeouts, then measures correct ID matching and error handling.
topics.name: MCP JSON-RPC Client
topics.real_world_use: Agent frameworks implement JSON-RPC clients to talk to tool servers.

topics.concept: An MCP session spans the connection lifecycle: initialize with capability negotiation, exchange messages, then shut down cleanly. Session IDs scope state, and re-initialization recovers from dropped transports. The manager simulates seeded sessions with capability matrices and reconnect drills.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded client-server sessions with capability negotiation and injected disconnects, measuring recovery success.
topics.name: MCP Session Manager
topics.real_world_use: Agent hosts manage long-lived server sessions across user conversations.

topics.concept: The stdio transport runs the server as a child process and speaks JSON-RPC over its standard input and output: simple, local, and the default for desktop integrations. Message framing uses newline-delimited JSON, and stderr carries logs separately. The simulator spawns a seeded mock server process and exchanges messages.
topics.data_idea: Spawns seeded mock server processes and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages, measuring round-trip latency and framing errors.
topics.name: MCP Stdio Transport Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Desktop assistants launch local tool servers as child processes over stdio.

topics.concept: The SSE transport serves remote MCP servers over HTTP: clients POST JSON-RPC requests and receive streamed responses as server-sent events. It suits hosted servers that many clients share, with auth headers on every request. The simulator models seeded HTTP exchanges with streaming response chunks.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded HTTP request-response cycles with SSE streaming chunks and injected network delays, measuring stream completion.
topics.name: MCP SSE Transport Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Hosted tool platforms serve many agent clients over HTTP streaming.

topics.concept: Tool schemas are the contract between model and tool: JSON Schema types, required fields, enums, and descriptions guide the model to produce valid arguments. Overly loose schemas invite bad calls; overly strict ones reject valid ones. The designer validates seeded schemas against sample calls and scores schema quality.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded tool schemas and argument samples with known validity, then scores schema precision and recall on the samples.
topics.name: MCP Tool Schema Designer
topics.real_world_use: API teams design tool schemas so models call their endpoints correctly.

topics.concept: Sampling lets a server ask the client to generate text: the server sends a sampling request, the client's model produces a completion, and the server continues its work. This inverts the usual direction so servers can use model intelligence mid-tool. The bridge simulates seeded sampling round trips with context limits.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded server-initiated sampling requests with token budgets and measures round-trip success and truncation rates.
topics.name: MCP Sampling Bridge
topics.real_world_use: Smart tool servers request model help for summarization mid-workflow.

topics.concept: Roots define the filesystem or URI boundaries a server may access: clients declare which directories are in scope, and servers must refuse paths outside them. Multiple roots support multi-project workspaces, and root change notifications let servers refresh. The manager enforces seeded root policies on path requests.
topics.data_idea: Defines seeded root scopes and tests path requests inside and outside them, measuring correct allow and deny decisions.
topics.name: MCP Roots Manager
topics.real_world_use: Code assistants scope file access to the open project folders.

topics.concept: Elicitation lets a server request structured input from the user through the client: the server sends a schema, the client renders a form, and the user's answers come back validated. It keeps sensitive input handling on the client side. The simulator runs seeded elicitation flows with validation retries.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded elicitation requests with schemas and user answer patterns, measuring validation pass rates and retry counts.
topics.name: MCP Elicitation Flow Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Agents collect credentials and confirmations through structured user prompts.

topics.concept: MCP logging routes server logs to the client: servers send log notifications at levels from debug to emergency, and clients filter by minimum level. Structured log fields make machine filtering possible. The channel simulates seeded log streams and tests level filtering and routing.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded log events across severity levels and routes them through level filters, measuring delivery and drop rates.
topics.name: MCP Logging Channel
topics.real_world_use: Agent dashboards stream tool-server logs for debugging.

topics.concept: Long tool calls report progress so clients can show spinners instead of hanging: servers send progress notifications with completed and total counts, and clients aggregate across parallel calls. Cancellation tokens let users abort stuck operations. The tracker simulates seeded long calls and aggregates progress streams.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded long-running tool calls emitting progress events and aggregates them into per-operation completion percentages.
topics.name: MCP Progress Tracker
topics.real_world_use: File-operation tools report progress during long transfers.

topics.concept: Cancellation stops in-flight requests: clients send cancel notifications, and servers must halt work and release resources promptly. Idempotent handlers tolerate duplicate cancels, and timeouts bound how long a cancel takes. The simulator injects seeded cancellations and measures stop latency and cleanup.
topics.data_idea: Runs seeded long requests with cancellation injected at random points and measures stop latency and resource cleanup success.
topics.name: MCP Cancellation Flow Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Interactive agents let users stop runaway tool calls.

topics.concept: A multi-server hub connects one client to many MCP servers: tool names are namespaced per server to avoid collisions, and routing policies pick the right server per call. Aggregated discovery presents a unified tool list. The hub simulates seeded servers and measures routing correctness under name collisions.
topics.data_idea: Registers seeded tools across servers with intentional name collisions and tests namespaced discovery and routing accuracy.
topics.name: Multi-Server MCP Hub
topics.real_world_use: Agent platforms aggregate dozens of tool servers behind one client.

topics.concept: Auth gateways protect MCP servers: clients present tokens on connect, the gateway validates scopes per tool, and expired tokens trigger re-authentication flows. Scope-per-tool means a file-read token cannot call a payment tool. The gateway simulates seeded auth exchanges with scope checks.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded connect attempts with valid, expired, and under-scoped tokens and measures correct allow, deny, and re-auth decisions.
topics.name: MCP Auth Gateway Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Enterprise tool servers gate agent access with scoped tokens.

topics.concept: Tool approval gates pause sensitive tool calls for human confirmation: the client shows what the tool will do, the user approves or denies, and the decision is logged for audit. Policies auto-approve low-risk reads while always gating writes and external actions. The gate simulates seeded approval flows with risk tiers.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded tool calls across risk tiers and simulates approval decisions, measuring auto-approve accuracy and audit completeness.
topics.name: MCP Tool Approval Gate
topics.real_world_use: Agent products ask permission before tools modify files or send data.

topics.concept: Capability negotiation happens at session start: client and server exchange the features they support, such as tools, resources, sampling, and roots, and each side only uses the intersection. Version mismatches fall back to the common subset. The negotiator simulates seeded capability matrices and computes effective feature sets.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded client and server capability sets with version skew and computes negotiated intersections plus fallback behavior.
topics.name: MCP Capability Negotiator
topics.real_world_use: Mixed-version agent fleets negotiate common features at connect time.
